actors.notes: Russia's SVR-linked group. Spear-phishing via compromised diplomatic email accounts and innovative device-code authentication phishing lures for M365 token capture [#9 Champion]; credential and token abuse for persistent access to email, cloud storage [#4 High]; Cobalt Strike deployment [#7]; SolarWinds supply chain history [#10 High]. Targeted French embassies, TeamViewer corporate IT, Microsoft, and US government-adjacent organizations. Storm-2372 designation for device code phishing campaign active since Aug 2024.

Russian GRU group operating BadPilot campaign. Opportunistic exploitation of exposed network devices at near-global scale since 2021 [#2 High]; custom persistence mechanisms [#7 High]; extensive abuse of legitimate RMM tools (Splashtop) and Signal's linked-device feature for message interception [#1 High]; malicious QR codes for Signal compromise [#9 High]; close-access operations using battlefield-captured devices in Ukraine context [#8 Medium]. Devices in Switzerland specifically targeted per Microsoft mapping. Historical sabotage capability (NotPetya, Industroyer).

Russian intelligence-linked group. Innovative two-stage WhatsApp spear-phishing: first email contains intentionally broken QR code, follow-up provides valid QR code linking attacker device to victim's WhatsApp [#9 Champion]; WhatsApp account takeover via linked-device feature abuse [#4 High, #1 Medium]. Impersonated US government officials and targeted individuals linked to the Ukraine conflict. Campaign terminated November 2024. Demonstrates constant capability development.
sources: Microsoft Security Blog (Star Blizzard WhatsApp campaign)

actors.notes: PRC MSS-affiliated actor. Exploited BeyondTrust zero-days to breach US Treasury [#2 High]; abusing stolen API keys and PAM credentials [#4 High]; targeting IT supply chain organizations to reach downstream customer environments [#10 High]; abusing cloud configurations and ORB covert networks [#1 High]. Linked to Yin Kecheng (Shanghai), sanctioned by US Treasury OFAC Jan 2025. USDOJ indictments March 2025.

PRC MSS-affiliated actor targeting global telecoms. Exploited CVE-2023-20198 and CVE-2023-20273 in Cisco IOS XE at scale, ~1,000 devices attempted Dec 2024–Jan 2025 [#2 Champion]; telecommunications interception capability for intelligence collection [#5 High]; persistent long-term access to telecom infrastructure [#1 High]. Linked to Sichuan Juxinhe Network Technology, sanctioned by US Treasury. Devices in Switzerland targeted per Recorded Future mapping.

China-nexus group with 3-year persistent compromise of East Asian company. Abused F5 BIG-IP load balancers and exploited CVE-2024-20399 (Cisco NX-OS) for edge-device footholds [#2 High]; deployed PlugX RAT in two forms — external C2 variant and internal lateral-movement variant [#7 High]; Impacket for credential harvesting and lateral movement [#4]; leveraged out-of-date F5 devices as persistent footholds [#1].

China-nexus actor specializing in network infrastructure and virtualization exploitation. Zero-day exploits against VMware ESXi and Juniper Junos OS routers [#2 Champion]; Linux rootkits, VMCI backdoors, custom TINYSHELL-based implants on routers [#7 High]; SSH and TACACS+ credential sniffing [#4]; redundant persistence across hypervisors, VMs, and network devices, leveraging ORB networks [#1 High]. Targets end-of-life hardware lacking security monitoring. Juniper advisory refers to this activity as RedPenguin.

China-nexus actor focused on VPN appliance exploitation. Exploited CVE-2025-0282 in Ivanti Connect Secure [#2 Champion]; RESURGE malware (evolved from SPAWNCHIMERA/SPAWNSLOTH) with reboot survival, web shell creation, and boot disk manipulation [#7 High]; credential harvesting and account creation via web shells [#4]; manipulated integrity checks and modified system files for persistence [#1 High]. CISA malware analysis report issued.

China-linked group sharing ANEL/UPPERCUT backdoor with APT10. Spear-phishing with Expo 2025 lures targeting Central European diplomatic institute [#9 High]; phishing emails with client-side exploits [#3 Medium]; ANEL/UPPERCUT backdoor and customized AsyncRAT deployment [#7 High]. Operation AkaiRyu identified by ESET. Previously focused on Japanese targets, now expanding to European diplomatic entities.

China-linked espionage group that uniquely deploys ransomware for distraction, misattribution, or evidence destruction. Network intrusion for initial access [#2]; long-term credential access during espionage phase [#4]; CatB ransomware deployed at end of operations [#7 High]. Blurs the line between espionage and financially motivated crime, complicating attribution. Targeted the Presidency of Brazil, Indian healthcare, and critical infrastructure in Asia.

North Korean state-sponsored group. Fake job interview campaigns (ClickFake Interview) on LinkedIn targeting crypto and defense professionals [#9 Champion]; GolangGhost backdoor (Windows/macOS), FrostyFerret password stealer, heavily obfuscated loaders [#7 Champion]; FrostyFerret captures macOS system passwords, credential harvesting from corporate environments [#4 High]; ClickFix technique tricks users into executing malicious commands [#3 Medium]. TraderTraitor subgroup executed $1.5B Bybit ETH theft — largest crypto theft in history. Stolen assets dispersed across thousands of Bitcoin addresses.

North Korean group operating fake companies (C.C. Waterfall, StarGlow Ventures) on LinkedIn, freelancing networks, and Telegram to interact with victims [#9 Champion]; custom malware loaders, malicious games, trojanized PuTTY, Qilin ransomware payloads [#7 High]; publishes malicious npm packages for targets to install [#10 High]; credential harvesting through fake interactions [#4]. First observed nation-state actor deploying RaaS (Qilin) payloads — blurring state/criminal lines. Overlaps with Diamond Sleet and Onyx Sleet.

Conti-lineage ransomware group active since 2022, one of the principal TAs by victim count. Exploits VPN and edge-device vulnerabilities for initial access [#2 High]; credential abuse and rapid lateral movement [#4 High]; evolved multi-threaded ransomware with disk drive control, process management, and file encryption [#7 Champion]; data exfiltration with legitimate tools [#1]. Relationships with BlackByte, LockBit, Snatch. Rose to fill the post-LockBit/ALPHV vacuum. Consistently observed in Switzerland since May 2023 across all four reporting periods.

Conti successor group (Cardinal / Storm-1811 / UNC4393). BRUTED automated brute-forcing framework for credential stuffing against edge devices — Cisco, Fortinet, Palo Alto, SonicWall, WatchGuard, Citrix [#4 High]; phishing campaigns confirmed in leaked internal Matrix chat logs [#9 High]; exploited CVE-2024-26169 (Windows Error Reporting) as possible zero-day [#2]; Cobalt Strike, Brute Ratel for C2, ransomware deployment [#7 High]; EDR evasion [#1]. Internal communications leaked (Sept 2023–Sept 2024). Key members: Trump/GG/AA (Oleg Nefedovaka), Lapa, Cortes, YY.

Dominant RaaS that rose to fill the LockBit/ALPHV vacuum (launched Feb 2024). Rapid weaponization of zero-days in public-facing applications [#2 High]; first group to deploy EDRKillShifter using BYOVD technique to disable endpoint defenses [#1 High]; ESXi-specific encryptor (C++, derived from Knight), Windows/Linux versions (Go), ChaCha20+Curve25519 encryption, intermittent encryption for speed [#7 Champion]. Attacked Swiss cloud provider Ilem Group (Geneva, Jan 2025) affecting ~15% of 200+ customers. 600+ firms globally in 2024.

RaaS operator. Claimed zero-day exploitation for initial access [#2]; ransomware deployment and data exfiltration [#7 High]; credential use for lateral movement [#4]. Caused critical incident at London hospitals via Synnovis pathology provider (June 2024). Notable for being first RaaS to partner with a nation-state affiliate — North Korean Moonstone Sleet deploys Qilin payloads.

Conti-lineage ransomware group. Fake IT support calls to gain unauthorized access at car dealerships [#9 High]; ransomware deployment [#7 High]; supply chain amplification — attack on SaaS provider CDK Global cascaded to 15,000+ downstream car dealerships [#10 Medium]. Also hit NHLS South Africa (healthcare) and Kadokawa Japan (media).

RaaS distinct from MedusaLocker and Medusa mobile malware. EDR killer tools (EDRKillShifter, EDRSilencer, etc.) using BYOVD to disable endpoint defenses [#1 High]; phishing for initial access [#9 High]; credential-based initial access [#4]; ransomware with 300+ victims as of Feb 2025 [#7 High]. Joint CISA/FBI advisory issued (aa25-071a). Broadly targets critical infrastructure.

China-based ransomware group exclusively exploiting known CVEs on internet-facing servers with outdated software/firmware [#2 Champion]; rotating ransomware payloads and file extensions to evade detection [#7 High]. No social engineering, no phishing — purely vulnerability-driven. Organizations across 70+ countries affected. CISA advisory AA25-050A issued. Targets entities with poor patching hygiene.

Russia-attributed data extortion group specializing in mass exploitation of managed file transfer platforms. Serial zero-day exploitation of MFT solutions — MOVEit, GoAnywhere, now Cleo [#2 Champion]; data exfiltration tooling without traditional encryption [#7 High]; mass data theft for extortion [#1]. Notable that fraudsters have been observed impersonating Cl0p to send fake extortion demands to uninvolved organizations.

Russian nationals operating the Phobos ransomware variant under the 8Base brand. Phishing for initial access [#9]; Phobos ransomware deployment [#7 High]; data exfiltration using legitimate tools [#1]. At least 17 Swiss companies hit between April 2023 and October 2024. Operation Phobos Aetor: 4 Russian nationals arrested in Thailand (Roman Berezhnoy, Egor Nikolaevich Glebov, and others), 27 servers taken down by Europol.

Dual ransomware/hacktivist group with AI-assisted tool development. AI-generated ransomware encryptor [#7 High]; DDoS tools [#6 Medium]; JQRAXY_HVNC remote desktop tool and funkgenerate password tool [#4]; data brokering [#1]. Likely novice actors leveraging AI to iterate rapidly despite limited technical expertise. 85+ victims claimed by late 2024. Recycled leaked hacktivist data to inflate credentials. Represents the convergence of hacktivism, RaaS, and AI-assisted development.

Novel ransomware-without-malware technique. Uses stolen/compromised AWS credentials [#4 High] to weaponize AWS's native SSE-C (Server-Side Encryption with Customer-provided keys) feature to encrypt victim S3 data with attacker-controlled key [#1 Champion]. Recovery is impossible without the attacker's key. Classifies purely as #1 Abuse of Functions — no ransomware binary (#7) is deployed. Demonstrates how native cloud features can be weaponized for extortion.

English-speaking financially motivated group (overlaps with 0ktapus, Octo Tempest, Scatter Swine). Social engineering and help-desk manipulation for initial access [#9 Champion]; SaaS credential theft and permissions abuse for lateral movement [#4 High]; data theft via cloud synchronization tools, persistence on virtualization platforms [#1 High]. Active since May 2022, leverages underground Telegram communities for tools and services. Adapted tactics to focus on SaaS/cloud environments.

Phishing-as-a-Service platform operated by Arabic-speaking actor MRxC0DER. Phishing emails with PDF/QR code lures impersonating Adobe, Microsoft, HR departments [#9 Champion]; Adversary-in-The-Middle (AiTM) proxy intercepting 2FA codes in real-time [#5 High]; credential and 2FA token harvesting [#4 High]. Previously operated as Caffeine PhaaS. Targets financial institutions and Microsoft 365 accounts. Represents growing sophistication of PhaaS platforms enabling MFA bypass.

EU-focused Phishing-as-a-Service platform. Phishing with localized banking templates for 54+ financial institutions, SIM swapping [#9 Champion]; real-time credential and OTP interception [#5 High]; credential, OTP, and PhotoTAN capture [#4 High]. Operated by 'Vssrtje', launched March 2023, with 1,250+ Telegram members. Cash-out via money mule network. Specifically targets EU banking customers and e-commerce.

Russian-speaking stealer-as-a-service ecosystem. ClickFix, Fake Captcha, and fake Reddit site lures [#9 High]; victims download and execute malicious payloads from compromised CH websites and GitHub releases (trusted platform abuse) [#3 High]; LummaStealer infostealer delivers additional payloads — SectopRAT, Vidar, Cobalt Strike beacon [#7 High]; credential theft and exfiltration [#4]; GitHub release infrastructure abuse [#1]. Most actively distributed infostealer in Switzerland (Jan–Feb 2025).

Data broker group. Exploited CVE-2022-40684 zero-day in FortiGate devices to harvest configuration files, IP addresses, and VPN credentials (some in plaintext) from 15,000+ devices [#2 High]; massive credential dump [#4 High]; exfiltrated config files, private keys, firewall rules [#1]. Released entire dump for free on a Tor website as self-promotion. Swiss FortiGate devices included in the dump.

Unnamed state-level espionage actor. Emails disguised as invitations from organizers of a scientific/expert forum [#9 High]; zero-day Chrome sandbox escape CVE-2025-2783 chained with additional RCE exploit [#3 Champion]; related vulnerability CVE-2025-2857 subsequently found in Firefox. Targeted Russian media outlets, educational institutions, and government organizations. Discovered by Kaspersky.

Most prolific pro-Russian hacktivist group. DDoS attacks using custom DDoSia botnet [#6 Champion, #7 Medium for botnet component]. Targeted Swiss government during Ukraine Peace Summit (June 2024), Swiss infrastructure during WEF Davos (January 2025), and French infrastructure. Only limited, short-term effects observed as recommended mitigations proved successful. Attacks shift to other European targets after political events conclude.

Pro-Palestine, religiously motivated hacktivist group. DDoS attacks causing ~45 min disruption to Swiss Federal Administration — telephony, Outlook, websites, and specialized applications (Jan 10, 2025) [#6 High]. Previously disrupted Migros Bank ATMs, website, e-banking, and phone service (Jan 6, 2025). Motivated by Swiss face-covering ban (burqa ban) effective Jan 1, 2025. Previously targeted German organizations over Israel support.

Hacktivist group representing a concerning evolution beyond traditional DDoS. DDoS attacks remain primary method [#6 High]; but also deploying ransomware and info-stealing malware [#7 Medium, #9 Medium]. Represents the convergence of hacktivism with cybercrime — blending ideological motivation with destructive and financially motivated tooling. Geopolitically motivated, pro-Russian alignment.

Collaborating pro-Ukrainian hacktivist groups targeting Russian state and private companies. Phishing emails with exploits for initial access [#9 High]; client-side exploitation [#3 Medium]; shared CobInt backdoor, PowerShell C2 scripts (mcdrive.ps1), and tunneling scripts [#7 High]; compromising contractors to reach target infrastructure [#10 Medium]; shared C2 infrastructure [#1 Medium]. Notable for cross-group collaboration — distinct groups sharing tools, backdoors, and infrastructure.
